description: Narrow the frontend exfiltration-URL redaction (website/src/utils/sanitize.ts::sanitizeExfiltrationUrls) so legitimate long/query-heavy URLs at a narrow, code-owned exact-host allowlist stop being redacted, WITHOUT reopening the exfiltration hole for arbitrary hosts. This mirrors the STRUCTURE of the backend's _exfil_url_warning: split the checks into an UNCONDITIONAL tier (heavy percent-encoding + hard credential markers, applied to every host) and a HEURISTIC tier (the base64-blob/aggregate-query-length checks) that is skipped ONLY for an exact-match host allowlist. Chosen policy (the open design question the issue raises): use a code-owned exact-host allowlist containing exactly the two confirmed-benign hosts from the issue — `github.com` and `monitorportal.amazon.com` — matched case-insensitively and EXACTLY (no suffix match, so a look-alike like `github.com.evil.example` is NOT exempt). The allowlist skips ONLY the base64-blob and aggregate-length heuristics; the heavy-percent-encoding detector and the credential markers (AWS key id, ssh/PEM headers, Slack token) stay unconditional for every host including the exempt ones. Rationale for this over the alternatives: exempting ALL well-formed https URLs would delete the XPIA exfiltration guard entirely (an agent-emitted `?body=<base64 conversation>` is structurally identical to a benign prefilled issue link); a user-confirmed reveal UI is a much larger cross-cutting change out of scope for this fix; wiring the frontend to the backend's companion-supplied exempt_hosts is not possible in the browser (that set comes from a server-side CredentialPolicy the frontend has no access to at render time). A narrow code-owned host list is the minimal defensible narrowing that matches the backend's already-reviewed posture. IMPORTANT Safari-14 constraint: introduce NO regex lookbehind at module scope; use plain string/array membership and existing regex shapes. Do NOT touch CRED_PATTERNS (the JWT parity-pinned patterns).
steps: In website/src/utils/sanitize.ts, above sanitizeExfiltrationUrls, add a code-owned exact-host allowlist constant, e.g. `const EXFIL_EXEMPT_HOSTS = new Set(['github.com', 'monitorportal.amazon.com'])`. Add a comment block explaining: these hosts skip ONLY the base64-blob/length heuristics (not the percent-encoding or credential-marker checks); match is exact + case-insensitive (RFC 4343), never suffix; and cite issue #7820 as the reason. Keep the list intentionally tiny and code-owned (not config-driven) so the agent cannot widen its own trust.

Carve the current combined EXFIL_PATTERNS into two regexes so the unconditional tier can run independently of the exempt hosts, mirroring the backend's _EXFIL_PERCENT_RE / _HARD_CREDENTIAL split: (a) EXFIL_PERCENT_RE = /%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}(?:%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}){20,}/i for heavy URL-encoding (20+ CONSECUTIVE octets); (b) EXFIL_CREDENTIAL_RE covering the hard credential markers currently in EXFIL_PATTERNS — (?:AKIA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}, (?:ssh-rsa|ssh-ed25519)[\s+%], BEGIN[\s+%](?:RSA|DSA|EC|OPENSSH)[\s+%]PRIVATE[\s+%]KEY, xox[bpas]-[0-9a-zA-Z-]+ — case-insensitive. Keep the base64-blob alternative [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,} as its own EXFIL_B64_RE (the heuristic tier). Preserve the exact regex fragments/flags already present so behavior for non-exempt hosts is unchanged; do NOT use lookbehind anywhere.

Rewrite sanitizeExfiltrationUrls to mirror the backend layering per matched URL: (1) compute lowercased host from m[1]; (2) if the query (path+query after '?') is empty, continue as today; (3) UNCONDITIONAL: if EXFIL_PERCENT_RE.test(query) OR EXFIL_CREDENTIAL_RE.test(query) -> redact (regardless of host); (4) HEURISTIC (base64-blob + aggregate length): compute `const isExempt = EXFIL_EXEMPT_HOSTS.has(host)`; if NOT exempt and (query.length >= EXFIL_QUERY_MIN_LEN OR EXFIL_B64_RE.test(query)) -> redact. Reset .lastIndex on any reused /g or stateful regex before each .test to avoid the sticky-lastIndex bug (note URL_RE is already reset via matchAll; the new tier regexes should be non-global or reset before test). Keep the redaction replacement string exactly as today: i18nT('utils.sanitize.redacted_suspicious_url', { domain }).

Confirm the change preserves current behavior for arbitrary hosts: a non-github/non-monitorportal URL with a >=200-char query or a 40+ base64 blob is STILL redacted; a heavy-percent-encoded or credential-bearing query is STILL redacted even at github.com/monitorportal.amazon.com.

Do NOT modify the credential patterns pinned by test_redaction_mirror_parity.py (the two eyJ... alternatives and CRED_PATTERNS). Verify no lookbehind ((?<= or (?<!) was introduced anywhere in the file.
acceptance_criteria: A github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/issues/new?title=...&body=...&labels=... URL whose query is >=200 chars but contains no credential markers and no 20+ consecutive percent-encodings renders UNCHANGED (not replaced by the redacted placeholder).
A monitorportal.amazon.com URL with a long benign query string renders unchanged.
An arbitrary host (e.g. https://evil.example/collect?data=<200+ chars>) is STILL redacted.

A github.com URL whose query contains an AWS key id (AKIA...), an ssh/PEM marker, a Slack token, or 20+ consecutive percent-encoded octets is STILL redacted (exemption does not cover the unconditional tier).
A suffix look-alike host github.com.evil.example is NOT treated as exempt (exact match only).
No regex lookbehind exists anywhere in website/src/utils/sanitize.ts; `cd website && npm run build` (or npx tsc -b) still succeeds.
test/test_redaction_mirror_parity.py still passes (JWT credential parity + no-lookbehind assertions).
verification: cd website && npx vitest run src/test/
findings: Implemented in website/src/utils/sanitize.ts. Carved the old combined EXFIL_PATTERNS into three module-level constants mirroring the backend split: EXFIL_PERCENT_RE (/%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}(?:%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}){20,}/i, unconditional heavy-percent), EXFIL_CREDENTIAL_RE (AWS key id / ssh-rsa|ssh-ed25519 / BEGIN...PRIVATE KEY / xox[bpas]-, unconditional hard markers), and EXFIL_B64_RE (/[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,}/i, heuristic base64 blob). All three are NON-GLOBAL so .test() has no sticky-lastIndex; URL_RE stays /g and is reset via matchAll. Added code-owned exact-host allowlist EXFIL_EXEMPT_HOSTS = new Set(['github.com','monitorportal.amazon.com']) with a comment citing issue #7820. sanitizeExfiltrationUrls now: lowercases the captured host, runs the unconditional tier (percent OR credential) for every host, then the heuristic tier (length>=200 OR base64) only when !EXFIL_EXEMPT_HOSTS.has(host). Redaction replacement string unchanged: i18nT('utils.sanitize.redacted_suspicious_url', { domain }). CRED_PATTERNS and the two eyJ JWT alternatives left byte-for-byte untouched. No lookbehind introduced (verified by grep for (?<=/(?<! -> 0 matches). Added website/src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts (10 tests) covering all acceptance criteria. TEST-DATA NOTE for future features: URL_RE's path/query group is [^\s)"'>]* so it truncates at whitespace; long benign query fixtures must percent-encode spaces (%20), not use literal spaces, or the captured query falls below the 200-char threshold and the >=200 test does not exercise the branch you think it does. Verification: `cd website && npx vitest run src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts src/test/sanitizeCredentials.test.ts src/test/MarkdownRenderer.sanitize.test.tsx src/test/sanitizeXss.jsdom.test.ts` -> 43 passed; `cd website && npx tsc -b` -> exit 0; `cd website && npm run build` -> built in ~24s, exit 0 (Safari-14 guard satisfied); `python3 -m pytest test/test_diagnostics.py test/test_redaction_mirror_parity.py test/test_security.py -q` -> 1243 passed, 1 skipped (parity + no-lookbehind assertions green). NOTE: the full `npx vitest run src/test/` suite exceeds the 120s tool timeout, so ran the sanitize/markdown/xss subset that exercises this module. Also added a concise frontend-mirror paragraph to docs/system-specs/modules/security.md under the URL exfiltration detection section.
